name: Why do I have low water pressure in my house?

mainEntity.name: Why do I have low water pressure in my house?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low water pressure can stem from several issues, including municipal supply problems, partially closed main water valves, or mineral buildup in pipes. It could also be a result of a faulty pressure regulator, a significant leak somewhere in your plumbing system, or even issues with your water heater. Identifying the exact cause often requires a systematic check of different components of your home's water supply system. If the problem affects all fixtures, it's likely a main supply issue or the pressure regulator. If it's isolated to one area, the problem might be localized.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low water pressure can be caused by municipal issues, closed valves, pipe buildup, faulty regulators, or leaks.
